text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The combination of a painful, ulcerative leg lesion with an ant bite trigger (pathergy), a history of inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's), diabetes, and recent corticosteroid use, alongside normal infectious workup (CBC, CRP, Culture) and negative autoimmune serology, strongly supports this clinical diagnosis.
